blocks.text: *Gear that shapes your skills, your defense, and your look.*
Weapons decide which skills you may use

Your weapon is more than a stat stick — its **type** decides which of the skills you have learned you may use right now (see *Skills*), and a forged weapon raises one of those skills through its **trademark** (below). Every weapon is a real 3D object your character holds.
The weapon roster

Every weapon owns a **distinct playstyle** — one clear reason to wield it. That playstyle isn't a design label: each of the twelve is the last surviving trace of one of the **Twelve Unwritten**, and how the weapon fights *is* how that person fought. None of them was ever named — only described by the deed witnesses remembered. They fall into three families:
Might — physical power, up close

rows: Win duels with precise single-target bursts and timed defense.
The One Who Cleared the Road
Delete whole groups with huge cleaves.
Deny enemies their turn — stun and knock them back.
The One Who Moved the Line
Reposition the fight — pull enemies in and impale them.
Protect your allies by absorbing all the attention. *(off-hand — pair it with a one-handed weapon)*

blocks.text: Finesse — precision & mobility

rows: Win through mobility and spacing — kite and never get touched.
Land one devastating shot, then reload.

blocks.text: Arcane — magic

rows: The One Who Burned the Field
Dominate whole areas with destructive magic.
The One Who Brought Them Back
Slowly overwhelm enemies with stacking curses.

blocks.text: Each weapon type has a deep pool of skills, but **a weapon carries none of them**. You learn a skill by practising that kind of weapon, and it is yours for good — what you hold only decides which of the ones you know you may use right now. See *Skills* for how they are learned.
Equipment slots
Beyond your weapon, you wear:
There is no ring slot: your **Ring** is part of you, not something you wear (see *Stats & the Ring*).
Each piece adds what its **folds** and its **quality** make it worth — attack on a weapon, defence on armour — plus any stats written onto it with **Ink** (see *Crafting & Recycling*).
Folds (+N)

The **+N** on a piece is how many times it has been **folded** at its station. Each fold costs one unit of the band material of the piece's own grade, plus gold, and adds one to what the piece is worth: **attack** on a weapon, **defence** on armour and a shield, **magic defence** on a garment, and one of each per two folds on a head piece. A staff gains magic attack instead of attack.

That fold total is then **lifted by the grade** — nothing at Raw and F, rising to **+30% at A**. So an A-grade piece at its full thirty-five folds carries 46 attack, where the same thirty-five folds on an E-grade piece carry 37.
**A quench spends every fold**, whichever way it goes. Folds are not lost work: half of what a finished piece cost comes back if you recycle it (see *Crafting & Recycling*).
Quality

Every piece you make carries a **quality grade**. A freshly forged piece is **Raw**; above that the ladder runs **F, E, D, C, B, A**, and A is the best there is. Quality is decided by the **quench** — the one moment of luck in a whole piece's making — and it moves one rung at a time, up or down, never in a jump.

**Quality decides five things.** How far a piece can be **folded**, which is what its attack or defence is made of; how much that fold total is **lifted**; how many **stats** can be written onto it with Ink; how far your **mastery** with it can go; and, on a weapon, how much its **trademark** raises its skill — **+5%** at Raw up to **+20%** at A. A fine blade does not swing harder by itself — it lets you become better with it than a poor one ever will.
Where a weapon's skills come from

**A weapon carries no skills.** You learn them yourself, by fighting with that kind of weapon: every skill names the **mastery level** at which it opens, and some name a skill you must know first. What you have learned is yours for good — the weapon in your hands only decides which of them you may use, and how much further you can still learn.

**A forged weapon has a trademark.** At the forge it rolls one skill of its type and is named for it — a sword that empowers Blade Dance is a **Ranbu**, and folded to +15 at grade C it reads **+15 Ranbu [C]** in your bag and on its card. The name never changes. Any skill of the weapon's pool that has a number to raise can come up: each ultimate one time in twenty, the others sharing the rest evenly. While you hold the weapon, **every** number that skill puts out is raised by **+5%** at Raw, rising with the grade to **+20%** at A — a Ranbu raises Blade Dance's strike and its damage buff alike. Hover the weapon to see which skill and which numbers; hover the skill to see the bonus on its own line.
So two people holding the same sword do not have the same skills: they have the skills they each practised for.
Cards
Some gear has **card slots** you can socket with cards for monster-matchup bonuses. See **Cards**.
